name: Lucky Bamboo
hook: Brown leaves on your lucky bamboo? Move it out of the sun.

steps.title: Bright, no direct sun
steps.tip: An east- or north-facing room is ideal. Direct sun turns the leaves brown.

steps.title: Fresh water every week
steps.tip: Keep the roots and at least 2.5 cm of stem underwater. Use chlorine-free water and change it weekly.

steps.title: Or grow it in moist soil
steps.tip: In soil, water when the top 2.5 cm is dry, let it drain, and never leave water in the saucer.

steps.title: Feed at quarter strength
steps.tip: In water, add ¼-strength liquid houseplant fertilizer every other month. In soil, feed monthly while it grows.

steps.title: Root a cutting in water
steps.tip: Cut a new shoot, strip its lowest leaves and stand it in water. Roots usually form in 2–3 weeks.

steps.title: Rinse off mites and aphids
steps.tip: Check for spider mites, mealybugs and aphids. Rinse the leaves, or use neem oil or insecticidal soap.

outro: Fresh water each week and soft, indirect light keep it green.

sources.title: Clemson HGIC: How to Grow and Care for Lucky Bamboo (Dracaena sanderiana)

faqs.question: Why are my lucky bamboo leaves turning yellow or brown?
faqs.answer: Yellow leaves and soft stems usually mean too much water in soil. Brown leaves point to direct sun, and brown tips to dry air.
